about: Editor spec §64 (GS8): the graph spec's axioms, the few laws every valid graph obeys. requirements/graph-spec.gql holds them as §28, each with its plain sentence, its formal line and the rules that rest on it; this table gives the library what it needs at run time. Each axiom has a stable problem code, GA and two digits, after the axiom it names, never reused (editor spec §42, problem_codes). checked says where a break is found: 'graph' means the check (axioms.js, and graphspec/rules/axioms.py) finds it in one graph; 'generated' means it is a law of an operation, such as a join, and the generated-graph tests hold it. packages/graph-spec/test/axioms.test.mjs holds this table to the spec file.

axioms.name: Identity
axioms.plain: Each thing has one id, and no other thing in its graph has it.
axioms.formal: id is one-to-one on the things of a graph
axioms.message: {place} is held under the name '{key}' but its id is '{id}'
axioms.fix: keep each thing under its own id

axioms.name: Links have two ends
axioms.plain: Every link starts and ends at a thing that is in the graph.
axioms.formal: for every link l: from(l) and to(l) are things of the graph
axioms.message: {place} has no thing at its {end} end, '{id}'
axioms.fix: write the thing it names, or take the link out

axioms.name: Declared types
axioms.plain: Every thing and every link has a type its schema declares.
axioms.formal: for every element e: type(e) is declared in schema(g)
axioms.message: {place} has the type {type}, which the schema does not declare
axioms.fix: declare {type} in the schema, or use a type it declares

axioms.name: Same text, same graph
axioms.plain: Reading is a function: the same text gives the same graph, and writing it out and reading it back changes nothing.
axioms.message: graph {graph} does not come back the same when it is written out and read again: {why}
axioms.fix: keep to values the flat projection can write, such as text, numbers, dates and true or false

axioms.name: SAME_AS is an equivalence
axioms.plain: A thing is the same as itself, same-as goes both ways, and it chains.
axioms.formal: SAME_AS is reflexive, symmetric and transitive
axioms.message: the things made one by SAME_AS do not form whole sets: {why}
axioms.fix: join SAME_AS links only through the one same-as function

axioms.name: Joins are order-free
axioms.plain: Graphs joined in any order, or joined twice, give the same graph, and the join loses and invents nothing.
axioms.formal: join is commutative, associative and idempotent, and keeps every statement
axioms.message: the join depends on the order of its graphs, or loses or invents something: {why}
axioms.fix: merge only through the join, never by hand

axioms.name: Certainty in range
axioms.plain: A likelihood is a word on the graph's scale, and a range never runs from high to low.
axioms.fix: use a word on the scale, with the lower word first

axioms.name: History is a chain
axioms.plain: An item has at most one successor, and following successors never comes back to the start.
axioms.formal: SUPERSEDES is a forest: at most one successor each, and no loop
axioms.fix: give each item one successor, and supersede only something older

axioms.name: Derived equals recompute
axioms.plain: Every cache, snapshot and derived element equals a fresh recompute from the source.
axioms.message: a derived value differs from a fresh recompute: {why}

axioms.name: Conflicts are kept
axioms.plain: A real clash becomes contested claims, and neither side is asserted.
axioms.formal: never assert p and assert not p
axioms.message: a clash was settled instead of kept: {why}
axioms.fix: keep both sides as contested claims
